html:
Egypt is the land of the lower Nile, in the northeast corner of Africa, where almost everyone lives in a narrow green valley and delta surrounded by desert. On the map it appears as ancient Egypt from 3000 to 700 BCE, and as the modern state from 1715 to now.

Around 3100 BCE the valley was united under one king, the start of the Early Dynastic period. Over the next three thousand years Egypt had:

  • the Old Kingdom, which built the Great Pyramid;
  • the Middle Kingdom, a time of classic literature;
  • the New Kingdom, an empire from Nubia to Syria under kings such as Thutmose III and Ramesses II;
  • a Late Period of foreign conquerors, Kushites, Assyrians and Persians.

Its writing, hieroglyphs, was in use for over three thousand years. After Alexander, Greek kings ruled, then Rome, then Byzantium.

The Arabs conquered Egypt in the 640s, and it slowly became Arabic speaking and mostly Muslim, with a large Christian Coptic minority. Cairo became the capital of the Fatimid caliphs and the Mamluk sultans. In 1517 the Ottomans took it.

Modern Egypt began after Napoleon's invasion of 1798. Muhammad Ali, an Ottoman officer, made himself master from 1805 and built factories, schools and a modern army. The Suez Canal opened in 1869, debt followed, and Britain occupied Egypt in 1882. It became nominally independent in 1922. In 1952 army officers overthrew the king, and Nasser nationalised the canal and built the Aswan High Dam. Army rule has largely continued since, broken briefly by the revolution of 2011.
